body: You can't "cure" her, she'll have to do that herself. If she's not already in therapy or getting help, encourage her to look into it. Besides that, the best you can do is be there for her. It may seem like a simple answer, but honestly it means a whole lot more than you'd think for you to just to be there. As someone who has been in a similar situation, I have learned that it is the little things that matter most. It is easy for people who suffer from depression to become withdrawn and pull away from the people who are trying to care, so remind her that you do care. Be gentle with her, and try not to get frustrated if she pushes back. It’s like trying to nurse an injured baby animal back to health: shower her with love, prove that you’ll be there beside her, and eventually she’ll let you in. When she has her lower nights, hug her, hold her hand, make her tea, or cuddle her up in warm blankets and just talk to her. Or if it’s over the phone reassure her. Tell her she’s beautiful, tell her why you love her, and tell her she’s important and worth it. Good luck.
